To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we identified 3 novel H‐2Db‐restricted MUC‐derived CTL epitopes, (2) these epitopes are processed and presented in a breast‐cancer cell line and (3) CTL induced by these peptides are able to lyse tumor cells pulsed with MUC1 peptides derived from breast‐carcinomas, but not with peptides derived from normal breast tissue

we have identified novel breast‐tumor MUC1‐associated peptides, which can induce a CTL reaction in mice, that can be recognized by CTL from breast‐carcinomas, and which are capable of lysing MUC1‐positive breast‐tumor cells in an MHC‐restricted manner.
the MUC1 protein is overexpressed in a spectrum of tumors and that the non‐TRA domains can be used for the induction of an MHC‐restricted cytotoxic T‐cell response against breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and characterizing novel HLA‐restricted MUC‐1 derived peptides that can be used as targets for immunotherapy of breast cancer.
the identification of novel MHC class I‐restricted CTL epitopes in the MUC1 protein.
the development of novel breast‐tumor antigens and the identification of their cognate HLA class I‐restricted CTL epitopes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MUC1 gene is not a breast cancer gene, but a breast cancer associated gene.
the MUC1‐related peptides are not suitable for use as a therapeutic vaccine in breast‐carcioma patients.
the HLA‐A0201 restricted epitopes of MUC1, identified by the authors, are promising targets for immunotherapy of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified three novel MUC1-derived peptides that are capable of inducing HLA-A2-restricted CTL responses.
we have demonstrated the existence of 2 novel HLA‐B7‐restricted MUC‐1‐derived CTL epitopes.
the non‐TRA MHC‐restricted peptides are more effective in inducing CTL than TRA‐restricted peptides.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we were able to show that there is a potential for MUC1‐based immunotherapy for breast cancer, but it is limited by the fact that MUC1 is not expressed in all patients and is not expressed at high levels in all patients that do express it.
MUC1‐specific CTL responses are possible in breast cancer.
we have identified 3 novel MUC1‐associated CTL epitopes that may be useful in immunotherapy of breast cancer.
